name: Turn a flat sustained drone into rolling shaker-style percussion: loop and crossfade a stable bar, re-envelope it into rhythmic hits with a transient-preserving time-stretch gate at a fast note rate, then low-cut, boost one tuned mid harmonic, layer an organic shaker texture, snap it with a transient shaper and add a short parallel bright room
goal: Recycle a pad/drone into tuned percussion without a drum source. Pick the steadiest, least peaky bar of the drone, loop it with short crossfades to avoid clicks, consolidate, then use a transient-preserving warp/stretch mode with a fast transient rate (the presenter starts at a 1/60-type rate for shaker speed) and reduce the per-transient sustain/envelope so each grid step becomes a hit. Add a fade-in, consolidate again, high-pass the lows, boost the strongest mid harmonic so the hit is in key (the presenter's was G#), layer a shaker/tambourine texture (less hold, more attack, a little decay, slight pitch, denser), add a transient shaper (attack up, sustain way down), tidy with EQ and finish with a short, bright, no-pre-delay room in parallel (~22 ms, mixed under the dry).

source.title: Crazy Percussions Out of a Pad in Serum 2
source.transcript_note: DAW-specific warp UI mapped to a generic transient gate.

prerequisites: DAW with a transient-preserving time-stretch mode and per-transient envelope (e.g. a Beats/transient mode), or Web Audio: a GainNode envelope retriggered on a 1/16–1/32 grid (implementation note)
Parametric EQ, transient shaper, texture/noise layer source, short room reverb on a parallel chain

inputs.name: drone
inputs.description: Sustained pad or drone with a steady section

inputs.name: hit_rate
inputs.description: Grid rate for the generated hits (fast for shaker)

inputs.name: key_harmonic
inputs.description: Harmonic to boost so the percussion sits in key

outputs.name: percussion_loop
outputs.description: Rolling tuned percussion loop rendered from the drone

outputs.name: fx_chain
outputs.description: EQ → texture layer → transient shaper → EQ → parallel room

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Spoken values only: fast transient rate (~'60 notes' wording), room ~22 ms with no pre-delay and little depth. Other moves are by ear.
Consolidate after warping so the gating is printed into the waveform before further processing.
Keep the low end cut; percussion of this type lives in the mids and tops.

steps.action: Find the most stable, least peaky bar of the drone and loop it. Crossfade at each loop join so there are no clicks, then consolidate to one file.

Set a transient-preserving stretch mode with linear behaviour, choose a fast transient rate for shaker speed, then reduce the transient sustain/envelope until each step becomes a short hit. Raise level, add a small fade-in, and consolidate again.
steps.expect: Drone becomes a rhythmic, dynamic percussive pattern

steps.action: EQ: high-pass the low frequencies that are not part of the percussion, then boost one or two mid harmonics so the part has a pitch that fits the tune or groove.
steps.expect: Hits have a clear tonal centre in the mids

steps.action: Layer an organic texture (tambourine/shaker-type) with less hold, more attack, a little more decay, slight pitch shift and higher density. EQ the texture to fill what is not poking through and reduce its decay.
steps.expect: Sounds like real shakers rather than gated noise

steps.action: Add a transient shaper: raise attack, remove a lot of sustain, adjust speed so it is snappy but not overdone.
Final EQ: bring up the gap left by processing, roll off extremes, and let the main harmonic breathe.
Put a very short bright room (no pre-delay, little depth, ~22 ms) on a parallel chain beside the dry signal and mix it under.
steps.expect: Hits gain depth without washing out

verification: Rendered loop shows distinct transient peaks on the grid where the drone was flat.
One mid harmonic dominates an analyser and matches the track key.
No clicks at loop joins or hit onsets.
Muting the parallel room reduces depth but keeps the rhythm intact.
